title: Multi-AZ GPU node group Terraform module with ASG <-> Karpenter fallback and health safeguards
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Deliver a Terraform module for Private (VPC) deployments that provisions GPU node groups across multiple AZs and supports two runtime modes: managed ASG-backed nodegroups (for strict capacity control and driver lifecycle) and Karpenter provisioners (for bursty/fast-scaling workloads). The module should include robust health probes, graceful upgrade/drain hooks, GPU driver bootstrap automation, mixed-instance support for cost-performance, and clear fallbacks so production workloads maintain SLOs when one scaling mechanism is degraded.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Module instantiates a Multi-AZ GPU node pool in a customer VPC with variables for AZ selection, instance families, and driver channel. 2) Toggle toggles between ASG and Karpenter mode without changing API surface. 3) Health checks (kube-probe + synthetic GPU workload) detect unhealthy nodes and trigger replacement. 4) Upgrade path: rolling upgrades safely drain nodes, evict KV cache, and reattach EBS volumes; no more than 10% capacity loss at any time. 5) Autoscaling failover: when Karpenter controller is unavailable, ASG-backed reserved capacity provides safety capacity; when ASG capacity saturated, Karpenter can be enabled as overflow (configurable). 6) Module includes example usage, variables.tf, outputs.tf and integration test harness that runs in a staging Private environment.
design_notes:
- Use separate TF submodules: cluster-integration, compute-pool, driver-bootstrap, and healthhooks.
- Driver bootstrap uses DaemonSet with image version pin and preflight checks; supports optional vendor drivers (NVIDIA, AMD).
- Healthhooks run a small synthetic job that allocates a tiny CUDA workload and verifies NVLink/driver visibility; failures escalate to k8s cordon+drain and ASG replacement.
- Implement lifecycle hooks for ASG to call a small health lambda (or instance profile agent) to delay termination until driver unload and KV cache flush complete.
- Karpenter Provisioner template constrained per-AZ to avoid cross-AZ pod scheduling surprises.
- Secrets (license keys, KMS ARNs) are passed via module inputs and never stored in state; recommended to use SSM or customer-managed KMS.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Decided to prefer ASG for stable reserved capacity and predictable latency; Karpenter will be supported as an overflow mode to reduce tail latency cost.
- Chose a synthetic CUDA probe vs relying solely on node-exporter metrics since GPU driver issues can present only under device allocation.
- Mixed instance types are enabled by default (p3/ g5 equivalents) because cost/perf varies by region; downside: extra complexity in scheduling and benchmarking.
- Avoided adding on-prem appliance-specific logic to keep module cloud-agnostic; on-prem adaptations can be layered in a separate wrapper.
implementation_plan: 1) Scaffolding TF module and submodules (week 1). 2) Implement driver DaemonSet + preflight image + probe job (week 2). 3) ASG integration: lifecycle hooks, termination coordination agent (week 2). 4) Karpenter templates and fallthrough policy (week 3). 5) E2E tests in private staging with 1 small customer workload (week 3-4). 6) Docs, example repo and rollout (week 4).
risks:
- Driver lifecycle bugs can cause failed drains leading to pod loss.
- Incorrect fallback tuning could cause cost spikes (overprovision).
- Multi-AZ networking and ENI limits differ by instance type; risk of asymmetric capacity.
- Complexity in testing mixed-instance spot interruptions with Karpenter in Private VPC.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: validate TF plan for multiple variable combos.
- Integration: deploy module into staged Private VPC, run synthetic CUDA probe across nodes, simulate driver failure and observe replacement.
- Chaos tests: kill Karpenter controller, saturate ASG capacity, ensure fallback preserves SLO for a low-latency endpoint.
- Upgrade test: bump node AMI/driver and verify rolling upgrade honors maxUnavailable and KV cache flush timeouts.
